subject.title: [Bug]: Native Talk button triggers OpenAI Realtime WebRTC call and fails with 500 when Realtime is not configured

question: Should Control UI browser Talk start from implicit OpenAI realtime credential availability, including OAuth/Codex fallback, or only after an explicit realtime readiness/preflight says the provider is usable for this user?
rationale: Current code and docs intentionally support implicit OpenAI OAuth/Codex fallback, while the report expects a local/non-Realtime Talk setup not to activate OpenAI WebRTC or the microphone; either direction changes user-facing setup semantics.

options.title: Gate on Gateway readiness
options.body: Disable or block browser Talk before microphone startup unless talk.catalog/readiness reports a usable realtime provider, while preserving whichever credential sources maintainers choose.

options.title: Keep implicit credential activation
options.body: Treat configured OpenAI API-key/OAuth/Codex realtime auth as enough to show/start Talk, and narrow follow-up work to clearer diagnostics for provider or API failures.

options.title: Require explicit realtime config
options.body: Only show or start browser Talk when talk.realtime is explicitly configured, accepting the upgrade and migration implications for existing implicit setups.

recommendation.title: Gate on Gateway readiness
recommendation.body: Disable or block browser Talk before microphone startup unless talk.catalog/readiness reports a usable realtime provider, while preserving whichever credential sources maintainers choose.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current-main ownership signal for the OpenAI Realtime credential fallback and docs that define this behavior.
